newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA SAYS PARALLEL DRUG IMPORTS WTO FRIENDLY.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA SAYS PARALLEL DRUG IMPORTS WTO FRIENDLY.

text.p: A proposed plan to introduce parallel importation of drugs to South Africa would not infringe the intellectual property rights of multinational drug companies, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Thursday.
Introducing the Intellectual Property Laws Amendment Bill in parliament, Erwin said parallel imports would be aimed at addressing pricing patterns "which cause considerable problems for us."
United States politicians have said the U.S. may consider taking South Africa to the Word Trade Organisation (WTO) if the legislation is seen as breaking intellectual property rights.

Parallel imports have been proposed in controversial new health reforms to allow South Africa to buy certain drugs made by multinationals operating in South Africa from other countries where they are sold more cheaply.
"It is important to understand that this provision would in no way infringe on our international obligations and, in our view, does not infringe on the property rights of companies," Erwin said.

Erwin said the bill reflected the fact that South Africa had "taken a very clear decision that it is our intention to be a country of best practice" in the recognition of trade marks and intellectual property rights.
"We should not underestimate the importance of this for protecting our own intellectual property rights," he said.

South Africa's drug industry has said that it is not fundamentally opposed to bringing in drugs from abroad as long as they undergo the same safety checks and registration process as locally made drugs -- with attendant costs.
